text: Good evening, detective. I'm Inspector Hart, and I'm glad you're here.
We have a case that needs a sharp pair of eyes.
Last night, Encik Rizal Hamid, the founder of Kite Design Studio, was found dead here, beside the front desk.
The gold Design of the Year award is gone from this display case, and the glass is smashed. That blinking outline is where it stood.
It looks like a break-in. But the doctor says he was poisoned. Four people had a reason to be here last night. Find who killed him, and prove it.
Last night, Datuk Hashim Karim, founder of the Heritage Gallery, was found stabbed to death in the Melaka Room, with the gallery's own keris.
He had found out that real pieces were being swapped for replicas. Bloody footprints lead from the body towards the entrance.
Four people had access to the room. Find who killed him, and prove it.
Search the room. When you find something important, pick it up or touch it, then tap Tag as evidence.
At the evidence board, choose the suspect who did it, pin the evidence that proves it, and submit. You can only submit once.
You're working alone on this one.
You're working with a partner. Talk to each other and decide together. Either of you can submit.
One more thing: don't step into the marked areas on the floor. They're part of the crime scene. And please don't run after anything you drop.
When you're ready, press Start. Good luck, detective.
Brilliant work, detective! You named the right person. Case solved!
Not quite, detective. The evidence pointed somewhere else.
Let me show you what really happened.
Twenty-one thirty-five. Grace Wong came back in from the rain, and signed in as G.W.
She made Encik Rizal a coffee, and stirred her sleeping pills into it, in her own Best Manager mug.
He drank it at the front desk. Minutes later, he slid off his chair, and never got up.
Twenty-one forty-two. She opened the case with her own staff code, and took the award.
Then she smashed the glass so it would look like a break-in, rinsed her mug, and hid it under the stand. The pawn shop email was her motive.
Eight-oh-five. Farid Rahman signed out the gallery key, as F.R.
The Datuk had found out about the replicas, and told Farid to meet him here at eight.
They argued. The vase went over, and the wall clock was knocked down. It stopped at eight seventeen.
Farid grabbed the keris from the plinth, and stabbed him.
In the struggle, the Datuk tore a scrap from Farid's scarf. Farid fled with the keris, leaving bloody footprints to the door.
That's the whole story. Thank you, detective.
